item: Genus-differentia. "A <term> is a <genus> that <differentia>." One genus, the nearest one; no categorizer words; no "and" or "or" in the genus; no circularity; no "usually" or "generally"; no examples or lists inside the definition; no evaluative or indexical words (Seppälä et al.

Small shared kernel. Terms that are truly the same across contexts go in a shared kernel: "Keep this kernel small", and it "shouldn't be changed without consultation" (Evans p. 31). A kernel term is a boundary object: "plastic enough to adapt to local needs ...
scope.md: Context: the repo or area this vocabulary governs, and its short context name
Build the checker script: Yes, after J1 and J3: a small script for T1 to T6 and T12, run in each domain repo

Kind and rigidity. Each term states its Kind. A role (sub-agent, reviewer) or a phase (draft, released) is never the broader term of a kind, and "can be a" is not "is a": OntoClean's own example wrongly puts *Agent* above *Animal*; "animals can be agents" (OntoClean §8.3).

Maintain (who: owner). Changes follow spec §9: anyone proposes a `candidate`, an agent approves it under spec G1 with Jonathan able to veto, every change is a named operation in `changelog.md` and the term's history, and nothing is deleted (Z39.19 §§11.3-11.3.2, pp. 96-97).
glossary.md: Definition: one sentence, genus-differentia (D1)

No permanent "other". Each facet has an Unsorted list, reviewed every round. A growing one means the structure is wrong: "The sure sign of a 'premature' hierarchical structure is the need for a 'miscellaneous' or 'other' category" (Kwasnik pp.

Heuristic review. At the end of a build round, check the evaluation questions of Z39.19 §11.2.2: unmarked synonyms, missing facets, out-of-date terms, consistent term form, quality of definitions and scope notes.
glossary.md: Kind: `thing`, `property`, `role`, or `happening` (S4)
When to run the process: Only when a domain is being worked in, inside that work; review monthly while active (proposal 9)
One principle per facet. Each facet uses a single characteristic of division, and its values are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive for the items in scope.
facets.md: Order: the order used for the values (by sequence, size, simple to complex, ...)

Collect the samples (who: model, checked by Jonathan). Collect "a representative sample of the entities. In a large domain, get enough to cover all foreseen possibilities. In a small domain, use the entire domain" (Denton §2.3 step 1). Items are files, sections or rules, whatever the competency questions are about.

Review. Review the unsorted lists and candidates at intervals set by how fast terms change (Z39.19 §11.3.1, p. 96), and at least whenever the domain is being actively worked on (J10). Shared-kernel changes need every affected context's owner (Evans p. 31).
Whose needs win: Jonathan's first, then the agents' (proposal 8)
glossary.md: Matches: see `map.md` (C3)

Labels. No label (preferred, alias or hidden) used twice in the context, after folding case and hyphens, counting deprecated records too (G5 keeps an old label on its deprecated record only); every deprecated record has a Replaced by that exists (SKOS S13-S14; potential duplicates, Z39.19 §11.4.6).

(Light version for small domains) One round of step 7 and the agreement test of step 8 on the held-back items, with two model families as raters (J6). With fewer than 30 items, kappa is recorded as indicative: it guides fixes but is not an ending condition (spec T8).
An item is a heading plus its opening text; raters sort the mechanism: Yes (M7)
(Light version for small domains) Steps 3 to 6 in one sitting on the remaining items.

An item is a section's heading and its opening text, and raters sort the mechanism. where items are sections of prose rather than catalogue rows, each item is the heading plus the first lines under it (up to about 300 characters), and the rater prompt says to classify the mechanism the section describes, not the doc it is in.

Three raters from three families, scored with Fleiss' and pairwise kappa. T8 uses three raters, each from a different model family, each the strongest model that family offers on Jonathan's plans at the time (for 2026-11: Claude, an OpenAI model through `codex exec`, and a Gemini Pro model through Antigravity's `agy -p`; not a Flash model).
scope.md: holds purpose, readers, owner, competency questions, out of scope, neighbours, ending conditions; required: yes
kind: a file of a domain folder

item: (Light version for small domains) Steps 0 and 1 as usual.
Three raters from three families, strongest model each; pass on Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 and the non-author pair's Cohen's κ ≥ 0.6: Yes (M4); Jonathan asked for OpenAI and a better Gemini on 2026-11-26

With three raters, the majority answer is the round's label. an item where two of three raters agree takes that value for T7; an item where all three differ goes to the facet's Unsorted list and is the first thing the next round's fixes address. Fixes still use the disagreements, not the majority.
Build a large domain in stages (kernel and areas, then one area at a time) inside one context: Yes (M1)

item: (Light version for small domains) Adopt when T1 to T7, T10 and T11 pass. Alexander's warning applies most here: keep it piecemeal and inside real work (Gabriel 2023, App. E.2).

item: Build a large domain in stages, inside one context. when a domain has more than about 300 candidate items or more than about six distinct areas, build it in stages. Stage 1 covers the kernel (the words every area uses) and one facet that sorts every item into an area.

A rater run through an agent CLI is kept to the prompt. when a rater is called through a vendor's agent CLI rather than an API (Jonathan's ChatGPT and Google AI plans have no API credit), run it in a new, empty directory, read-only, with tools and web access off where the CLI allows, the whole rater prompt as the only user input, and record the CLI name and version, the model, the reasoning effort and the date.

(Light version for small domains) Before building, hold back a third of the items (at least 10; if the domain has fewer than about 15 items, skip the held-out set and the kappa test altogether and rely on T7, T10 and T11).
Rules for a rater run through an agent CLI (empty folder, read-only, record CLI and model): Yes (M6)
With three raters, two-of-three is the round's label; three-way splits go to Unsorted: Yes (M5)
map.md: holds links to other contexts' terms and the shared kernel; required: once a second context exists
kind: a file of a domain folder

item: Test sample: at least 30, and at least 5 per value of the largest facet. each round's fresh sample is at least 30 items and at least five times the number of values in the largest facet. For prompts stage 1 (`area` has 8 values) that is 40; the domain uses 60, the round size J7 allowed for building.
Write the item unit and population down, and draw by a seeded rule. before drawing, `samples.md` states what one item is, which files the population comes from, the filters, and the seed.
changelog.md: holds every change as a named operation; required: yes
kind: a file of a domain folder
